rules.statement: Build the smallest complete system from the smallest sufficient, clean data model.

Start from the required outcome and accepted constraints. Settle the smallest sufficient data structures, ownership, valid states, invariants and failure behavior before choosing operations, abstractions, layers or file organization.
Build and verify the load-bearing behavior first, then require present necessity for every further addition.
Bind every type, field, variant and representation to a present requirement and the concrete failure its omission would cause.
Define each fact once with one authoritative owner. Derive values rather than store them when storage is unnecessary.
Omit speculative fields, APIs, abstractions, configuration, persistence, compatibility, concurrency and scaffolding.
Reject future usefulness, convention, elegance and flexibility as sufficient justification for adding anything.
Choose the complete solution with the fewest necessary concepts, owners, states and mechanisms.
Compare coupling, duplication, failure paths, public surface, testability and operational burden. Do not substitute line or file count for simplicity.
Reject a candidate when a credible complete alternative is no worse in every relevant complexity dimension and better in at least one.
Reduce mechanisms and effort, but never omit, defer, approximate or weaken an approved requirement to claim an efficiency gain.
